cases.assertions: Go Invoker cancellation reaches real CancelTask; native tool keeps its cleanup owner until an explicit barrier releases it. Concurrent production Abort cannot return before that join. Release closes all selected tools exactly once and removes the workspace.
An expired Stage request returns worker_timeout with zero model/tool charges, zero SDK model/tool callback entries and zero Gateway requests.

A dispatched tool advances the controlled loop beyond the semantic deadline. Exactly one model and one tool were admitted; no next provider or finalizer call occurs. Invocation remains pending while independent session cleanup is held, then returns worker_timeout after cleanup joins.

A completed native read settles history before its parallel write self-cancels. Go receives worker_task_cancelled and Worker State is cancelled, with one model, two tools, one tool error, known 7 input / 3 output / 10 total tokens, exactly one retryable tool_call_cancelled record and no extra first-invocation callback/provider/finalizer attempt. A healthy next shared invocation receives both original call/response IDs once, exact known sibling result and original logical invocation, without replaying either tool.

A controlled first cache-cleanup failure returns retryable allocation_cleanup_failed. A second allocation is rejected with non-retryable HTTP 409 allocation_conflict and the destroyed Worker is unavailable. Retrying the existing Release succeeds, closes selected tools once and removes the workspace.

The production LeaseWatchdog expires through controlled monotonic clock advancement and calls AllocationService.expire_control_lease. Native work remains owned until explicit join, before lease expiry finishes and real Release removes the workspace.

After the semantic deadline has expired, a separate cleanup timer is advanced past its five-second bound. The cleanup task is cancelled/joined, original worker_timeout remains the outcome, and the next invocation returns worker_draining before final release.
